notes: v1.14.580 — SW.JS STOPS ARGUING WITH ITSELF. Comments only: zero behaviour change, both skipWaiting() call sites byte-identical, verified by diffing every changed line as a comment. THE PROBLEM: the install handler carried TWO contradictory notes. A .458 block reading "the old note here read skipWaiting() at the end... that is no longer true and was the P0" sat DIRECTLY ABOVE a call to self.skipWaiting(), while .513's justification for that very call was stranded eighteen lines below at the bottom of the waitUntil block, far from the line it explained. A reader hit the .458 note first and concluded the call was a regression. THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT IS WHAT HAPPENED ON 2026-09-05, when the e2e suite's failing assertion plus the .458 comment together read as a live defect, and a fix was very nearly shipped that would have deleted the call .513 added to make upgrades land on the phone at all. THE FIX: the .458 note is DELETED — it documents a decision that no longer holds, and a superseded rule left in place next to the code that supersedes it is worse than no comment. .513's justification MOVES to the call site and now states the whole picture: why the call is there, that it overturns .458, what the trade is (the phone AUTO-UPDATES on install; the badge no longer owns promotion), the owner ruling of 2026-09-05 that .513 stands, and the fact that 39-sw-update-path.spec.js pins the .458 assertion with this reason so that an "expected to fail but passed" result is the signal this ruling needs revisiting. It also records that the message handler still exists and still promotes — .513 changed WHO triggers activation, not whether the message door works. NO CODE MOVED. self.skipWaiting() remains the first statement of the install handler and the message handler is untouched.
